patch_description: The previous program plateaued because hill-climbing on the global minimum is flat: most random moves don't change the min at all, so nothing is accepted. Following the recommendation, I rewrite the search to (1) target the argmin triangle directly — perturb only points that participate in one of the k smallest triangles, and use a *targeted geometric move* that pushes a vertex perpendicular away from the line through the other two vertices of its tiny triangle (the exact direction that increases that triangle's area), and (2) use a smooth acceptance score (mean of the k smallest triangle areas) so the optimizer receives gradient-like pressure on the whole "small triangle" set while the true global min is tracked separately as the gate for the best-so-far. Multiple deterministic initializations (regular 12-gon + center, radius-alternating ring + center, triangle-symmetric lattice, perturbed grid) are each annealed, then the overall best is polished by strict min-increasing local moves and rescaled so the convex hull has unit area. All area computations are fully vectorized over the 286 triples, keeping runtime ~1–2 s.
